newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CENTRAL/EAST EUROPE - NOV 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CENTRAL/EAST EUROPE - NOV 7.

text.p: Czech Republic:

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The governor of the Czech National Bank, Josef Tosovsky, will present Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus with a new proposal for the privatisation of the banking sector, according to Klaus.
- The governments of The Czech Republic and Ukraine have reached an agreement on cooperating to fight organised crime, terrorism and drug smuggling as well as a bilateral agreement on customs issues.
- Skoda has recieved approximately 9,000 orders for their new car, the Skoda Octavia. Sales of the car will begin on November 15th.

- The government rejected a proposal from the Ministry of Finance that the National Property Fund be allowed to hold tenders for companies in which it has minority stakes. Instead, a six-member committee has been formed with Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus at the head to decide on such matters.

- Representatives of Industry welcomed President Vaclav Havel's comments that the military should use traditional Czech armaments companies for the refurbishment of the military. While the original plan for the miltary's modernisation called for investments of 12 billion crowns annually between 1995 and 2005, it now appears that only half of this amount will be invested and some projects will be delayed.

- Zdenek Burian, the spokesman of Aero Holding, has stated that the plan proposed by the National Property Fund for removing Aero Vodochody's debts is unacceptable. According to Burian the NPF will decrease the value of the Holding company's shares if funds are given to Vodochody any other way than through the mother company.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - Boby Group and Boby Revue, two firms owned by Lubomir Hrstka, frequently called one of the richest men in the country, are threatened with bankruptcy proceedings. Albania:
The following are the main stories verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE

- The newspaper editorial said it was dangerous to politicise and limit the born crime in Albania with the idea it was done by the ex-communist secret police. The state should harshly react to the state corruption and crime craddle.
- People living in a wrecked bulding on Wednesday tell their terror after the explosion and complain their apartments were stolen by police forces controlling them later.
- Azem Hajdari, a ruling party MP, clashing with head of the independent trade union Valer Xheka on union's presidency.
- All political parties oppose a parliamentary committee compiles the new constitution as the ruling party says.
- Albanian countryside families greatly lack modern technology to work in their land property.
- Albanian lek became significantly strong on Wednesday reaching an exchange rate of below 100 leks per dollar.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- Trytol was used to wreck the apartment of the appeals court chief judge Prel Martini but in a greater amount than at Vefa compnay supermarket last February.
- Italian police blocked hundreds of ilegal Albanian emigrants and 114 kg of marijuana transported with powerful speedboats from the Balkan country to neighbouring Italy.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- Albanian President Sali Berisha congratulates Bill Clinton for his re-election and Boris Yeltsin for a speedy recovery after the operation.
- Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi and his deputy and Foreign Minister Tritan Shehu to participate at the Central European Initiative meeting in Gratz, Austria.
- Ibrahim Rugova, leader of the ethnic Albanians in the Yugosav province of Kosovo, congratulates Clinton for his re-election.
ZERI I POPULLIT
- Fatos Nano, the jailed leader of the opposition Socialist Party, wishes Clinton for his presidential victory.
Slovenia
- Slovenia's Constitutional court on Wednesday dismissed a request by Shell Slovenia to lift restrictions on the ownership of motorway petrol stations.
- Slovenia's Smelt Olimpija lost the sixth round basketball EuroLeague match against Greek Panathinaikos 76-74 on Wednesday.
- Slovenian Foreign Minister Davorin Kracun on Wednesday welcomed the outcome of elections In the USA, stressing good relations beetween the two countries during the previous Bill Clinton's mandate.
- About 70 foreign and more than 100 domestic journalists will cover the Sunday's general election, government's information office said on Wednesday.
- The government will discuss increase of electricity prices next week. The price would be lifted in two phases, each time for 10 percent, state secretary of trade said on Wednesday.
DNEVNIK
- This year more than 48,000 new students entered Slovenia's universities, which is 2,000 students more than in 1995.
- Doctor's Association of Slovenia said on Wednesday that this year 257 doctors applied to start private practice.
REPUBLIKA
- 770 companies have already finished their privatisation, while another 1,307 companies are still in the process, state secretary in charge of privatisation Edo Pirkmajer said on Wednesday.
Slovakia:

NARODNA OBRODA - Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said the ministry will prepare the final draft of the 1997 state budget by the end of this week. The law is expected to be presented to parliament by November 15.

- Marian Sasik, Secretary General of the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE), said the amendment to securities law, passed by the parliament on Wednesday, is a significant step back in the pace of development of the Slovak stock market, mainly in the field of protection of minority shareholders and the market transparency.
- Sasik also said the new legislation will prevent companies from obtaining financial resources on the capital market.
- President Michal Kovac will pay a two-day official visit to Netherlands, starting on November 12.

- A district court in the central Slovak town Banska Bystrica has rulled that independent daily Sme has to pay altogether 7.5 million crowns to 18 government members for violating their individual rights.
- The Russian airlines Aeroflot has canceled its regular route from Bratislava to Chicago, via Shannon in Ireland, and back due to lack of passangers.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said its restructuring procedures, started last year, have so far brough positive results in reducing the money supply and restructuring of the banks loan portfolios.

- The state fund of market regulation said it had already bought 250,000 tonnes of grain from this year harvest out of the planned amount of 400,000 tonnes. The fund said it would import 260,000 tonnes of fodder cereals this year and will sell for subsidised prices to prevent an increase in prices of related products.

- The Slovak chemical and pharmaceutical industry is expected to increase its exports by 10 to 12 percent by the year 2000. The industry imports currently account for around 24 percent of Slovakia's overall exports.

PRAVDA - Deputy Finance Minister Jozef Magula said the narrow group of owners of significant stakes in large companies and will seriously damage rights of small shareholders. -- Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-563-3687
